investigations.kind: Frame-level video analysis · three cameras, one camera original · V3
investigations.title: Two gestures before the shot
investigations.question: Did two men on the security line press something in the seconds before the shot, and try to hide it?
investigations.finding: Zero is the first frame in which Kirk's head and shoulders move abruptly (2.MOV 508, 16.mp4 185, 7.mp4 759), tied across the clips by their shared sound to 0.05 s; a larger head snap follows 0.2-0.37 s later. The plaid-shirt man's right hand leaves the barrier rail 0.30 s before that frame and his index finger is on his left sleeve 0.20 s before it, 50 ms before the first sound reaches that camera; no button, strap or device resolves at 1080p. The blue-shirt man's arms stay folded through it with the right hand hidden; the pocket under his arm is unchanged for 0.2 s after, then covered by Kirk's rising hand; the right fist emerges 0.47 s after. The white-polo man first taken for the sleeve-scratcher is holding a phone.
investigations.limitations: A hand out of view cannot be shown still. The anchor is a human reading of one frame per clip, checked by audio alignment to about 0.05 s and by a second person's movement. The plaid-shirt man is seen from one camera. No blinded rating was run; purpose is not addressed.

levels.observable_movement: yes, catalogued per frame for every hand in view
levels.identifiable_action: white-polo man: a phone; plaid-shirt man: none resolved (a finger on cloth); blue-shirt man: hand occluded, not observable

versions.label: V1
versions.note: Anchored on the loudest audio transient per file; in 2.MOV that was a crowd burst 2.25 s before the shot, which reversed the plaid-shirt finding. Withdrawn the same day; kept in git history.

versions.label: V2
versions.note: Anchored on Kirk's first visible movement per clip, cross-checked by audio cross-correlation between clips and by the blue-shirt man's movement in the 2.MOV foreground. Close-up loops added.

versions.label: V3
versions.note: Anchor moved from Kirk's larger head snap to his first abrupt head-and-shoulder movement, 0.2-0.37 s earlier, at the brief author's prompting; agrees with the audio alignment to 0.05 s and with study 02's markers to a few frames. Close-up loops reduced to three, the plaid loop with Kirk beside him.

investigations.kind: Independent review by ChatGPT Astra · four sources · reproduced with an editor's note
investigations.title: Movement and timing: a second review
investigations.question: What does ChatGPT Astra's separate review of the same files conclude, and where does it differ?
investigations.finding: Same frames, same observations. The review confirms sleeve contact at frames 487-492 of 2.MOV before Kirk's first movement and unfolding at 199-202 of 16.mp4 after it, resolves no control or object, and finds the folded posture 21 s earlier. Its zero in each file is within a few frames of study 01 V3's; study 01's first two versions disputed it and were wrong.
investigations.limitations: Frame brackets chosen by the reviewing model, no audio reference, no blinded rating. Reproduced in the review's own words; the editor's note was rewritten with study 01 V2 and the earlier note withdrawn.

versions.label: v1.0
versions.note: Package received as inputs/astra; boards and slowed clips kept unchanged.
